course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

quiz.title: Unit 2 LEQ: Comparing networks
quiz.headline: Comparing networks
quiz.promptTitle: Original Page One Unit 2 writing practice
quiz.prompt: Evaluate the similarities and differences in how two networks of exchange shaped economic and cultural life from 1200 to 1450.
quiz.instructions: Plan a defensible argument, then write one organized essay. This is a narrower Unit 2 practice task, not a full exam simulation.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice. Rubric feedback is self-assessment, not official College Board scoring.

responseFields.label: Essay response

responseFields.help: Informational word count only. No timer or automatic grading.

rubric.label: Thesis
rubric.guidance: Makes a defensible claim that answers the prompt and establishes a line of reasoning.

rubric.label: Contextualization
rubric.guidance: Explains a broader development that is relevant to the prompt and occurs before, during, or across the period.

rubric.label: Evidence
rubric.guidance: Uses specific evidence to support the argument; two points require more than one relevant example used as support.

rubric.label: Analysis and reasoning
rubric.guidance: Uses comparison, causation, or continuity/change reasoning and connects evidence to the claim with qualification where appropriate.

quiz.modelResponse: Annotated model for comparison: a defensible thesis names the relationship under evaluation; contextualization places the network in earlier Afro-Eurasian exchange; evidence uses specific places, institutions, or communities; analysis explains how geography, demand, politics, or culture produced the pattern and qualifies variation.
quiz.alternateModel: Another defensible route could center a different network or causal factor if it remains within 1200–1450, uses specific evidence, and explains why the evidence answers the prompt.
commonErrors: Listing three networks without a comparative or causal claim.
Using a famous example without explaining its relevance.
Treating the networks as sealed or uniform systems.
Using post-1450 European expansion as the main evidence.

scaffold.label: Claim

scaffold.label: Context
scaffold.text: Place the development in wider Afro-Eurasian history.

scaffold.label: Evidence

scaffold.label: Reasoning
scaffold.text: Show why the evidence proves the claim and where it needs qualification.
